description:
Goal

Give a root entry exactly one seed authority for Activation and ActivationInputs. SeedRoot owns the root contribution; SeedActivation must never reconstruct the same key from its arrow or leave a competing claim that survives root withdrawal.

Clarified ownership boundary

This is a sole-seeder law, not a sole-publisher law. AnalyzeActivation may legitimately publish the identical key when a self-recursive root reaches itself, and other callers may publish their own contributions. Those caller publishers and exact ActivationInputs evidence remain intact. The forbidden duplicate is SeedActivation competing with SeedRoot.

Correct-by-construction strategy

Record each canonical entry activation identity in the owning RootSlot at the World activation-key mint. Retain that ownership classification across temporary keying-fact withdrawal and actual later re-keying so a former entry key can never be reclassified as latent. Fact demands for every recorded entry identity route to SeedRoot. A distinct publisherless non-entry identity continues to route to SeedActivation. No display strings, rendered types, raw ordering, or global scans decide ownership.

Neighbor boundary

fz-kdt.64 explicitly owns the current grow-only ActivationInputs frontier. A rebased AnalyzeActivation can withdraw its Activation claim while its ActivationInputs evidence remains published; this ticket must preserve and characterize that rule, not bypass it or introduce contribution withdrawal. Either the remaining caller claim or the retained historical root classification prevents SeedActivation from reconstructing the key.

TDD acceptance

- Initial RED demonstrates root Activation and ActivationInputs demands route to SeedActivation instead of SeedRoot.
- Both root fact demands enqueue one seed authority and are co-owned by SeedRoot.
- Temporary InputDemand withdrawal does not change the recorded root ownership classification.
- A real keying-value change mints a replacement entry key; both the old and new identities remain root-owned, so a latest-only cache fails the test.
- A distinct publisherless activation of the same root function still uses SeedActivation.
- A self-recursive root proves AnalyzeActivation may legitimately co-publish the same key without SeedActivation ever running.
- Withdrawing SeedRoot preserves the legitimate caller claim and exact evidence. A real ground shift and rebased World conclusion withdraws the caller Activation claim while preserving ActivationInputs under the fz-kdt.64 frontier rule; neither fact demand may run SeedActivation or reconstruct root evidence.
- Agent docs and northstar describe sole seed authority rather than falsely claiming one total publisher.
- Focused tests, full library tests, strict Clippy, formatting, documentation tests, serial fixture matrix, and all-features CLI tests pass without increasing deterministic work baselines.
title: A root entry's Activation has two producers: SeedActivation reconstructs what SeedRoot owns
